disputes.reason: Claim that widening the bin 'roughly doubles the probability mass' only holds for the scenario's doubling of h (0.1 to 0.2); as a general statement about widening it is not judgeable, and it bundles a second claim about arbitrariness.

States the up-state rate is r0*e^sigma, which holds only for the scenario's zero drift and dt = 1; as a general fact about lognormal trees it is incomplete/false (up node is r0*e^(a*dt+sigma*sqrt(dt))).

'Holds more of the underlying' depends on the position hedged (short calls, as in the scenario); a long-call or short-put hedger would hold a larger short or smaller short position, so the statement is position-dependent and not judgeable standalone.

Same ambiguity: whether the BSM-delta hedger holds more or less underlying depends on the option position (short call vs long call/put); only the delta comparison is general, so a false label is not safe.

A conditional coverage test remains valid (and tests both coverage and independence) when exceptions are independent; 'appropriate' vs 'necessary' is arguable, so labelling it false is defensible either way.
